arxiv-2201-10211.title: An active-set method for sparse approximations Part I: Separable ℓ 1 \ell_{1} terms
arxiv-2201-10211.creator: Spyridon Pougkakiotis, Jacek Gondzio, Dionysios S. Kalogerias
arxiv-2201-10211.description: Abstract In this paper we present an active-set method for the solution of ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -regularized convex quadratic optimization problems. It is derived by combining a proximal method of multipliers (PMM) strategy with a standard semismooth Newton method (SSN).

arxiv-2206-00918.title: MEMD-HHT based Emotion Detection from EEG using 3D CNN
arxiv-2206-00918.creator: Monira Islam, Tan Lee
arxiv-2206-00918.description: Abstract In this study, the Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition (MEMD) is applied to multichannel EEG to obtain scale-aligned intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) as input features for emotion detection. The IMFs capture local signal variation related to emotion changes. Among the extracted IMFs, the high oscillatory ones are found to be significant for the intended task.

arxiv-2211-03476.title: Galactic Dynamos Journal: August 10, 2026 DOI: 10.1146/((please add article doi))
arxiv-2211-03476.creator: Axel Brandenburg 1,2,3,4 & Evangelia Ntormousi 5,6
arxiv-2211-03476.description: Abstract Spiral galaxies, including the Milky Way, have large-scale magnetic fields with significant energy densities. The dominant theory attributes these magnetic fields to a large-scale dynamo. We review the current status of dynamo theory and discuss various numerical simulations designed to explain either particular aspects of the problem or to reproduce galactic magnetic fields globally.

arxiv-2304-00423.title: Geometric constraints improve inference of sparsely observed stochastic dynamics
arxiv-2304-00423.creator: Dimitra Maoutsa
arxiv-2304-00423.description: Abstract The dynamics of systems of many degrees of freedom evolving on multiple scales are often modeled in terms of stochastic differential equations. Usually the structural form of these equations is unknown and the only manifestation of the system’s dynamics are observations at discrete points in time. Despite their widespread use, accurately inferring these systems from sparse-in-time observations remains challenging.

arxiv-2304-01680.title: Can BERT eat RuCoLA? Topological Data Analysis to Explain
arxiv-2304-01680.creator: Irina Proskurina, Irina Piontkovskaya, Ekaterina Artemova
arxiv-2304-01680.description: Abstract This paper investigates how Transformer language models (LMs) fine-tuned for acceptability classification capture linguistic features. Our approach uses the best practices of topological data analysis (TDA) in NLP: we construct directed attention graphs from attention matrices, derive topological features from them, and feed them to linear classifiers.

arxiv-2404-12359.title: Inverse Neural Rendering for Explainable Multi-Object Tracking
arxiv-2404-12359.creator: Julian Ost, Tanushree Banerjee, Mario Bijelic, Felix Heide
arxiv-2404-12359.description: Abstract Today, most methods for image understanding tasks rely on feed-forward neural networks. While this approach has allowed for empirical accuracy, efficiency, and task adaptation via fine-tuning, it also comes with fundamental disadvantages. Existing networks often struggle to generalize across different datasets, even on the same task.

arxiv-2506-15674.title: Leaky Thoughts: Large Reasoning Models Are Not Private Thinkers
arxiv-2506-15674.creator: Tommaso Green, Martin Gubri, Haritz Puerto, Sangdoo Yun, Seong Joon Oh
arxiv-2506-15674.description: Abstract We study privacy leakage in the reasoning traces of large reasoning models used as personal agents. Unlike final outputs, reasoning traces are often assumed to be internal and safe. We challenge this assumption by showing that reasoning traces frequently contain sensitive user data, which can be extracted via prompt injections or accidentally leak into outputs.

arxiv-2601-17269.description: Abstract In the present work, we analyze the properties of the transition form factors (TFFs) for the γ γ ∗ → η ( ′ ) \gamma\gamma^{*}\to\eta^{(\prime)} process, employing the η ( ′ ) \eta^{(\prime)} -meson light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) derived within the light-cone sum rule framework.

arxiv-2602-03025.title: RC-GRPO: Reward-Conditioned Group Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Tool Calling Agents
arxiv-2602-03025.creator: Haitian Zhong, Jixiu Zhai, Lei Song, Jiang Bian, Qiang Liu, Tieniu Tan
arxiv-2602-03025.description: Abstract Multi-turn tool calling is challenging for Large Language Models (LLMs) because rewards are sparse and exploration is expensive. A common recipe, SFT followed by GRPO, can stall when within-group reward variation is low (e.g., more rollouts in a group receive the all 0 or all 1 reward), making the group-normalized advantage uninformative and yielding vanishing updates.

pmc-10534868.title: First Principle Study on the Effect of Strain on the Electronic Structure and Carrier Mobility of the Janus MoSTe and WSTe Monolayers
pmc-10534868.creator: Jawad El Hamdaoui, Laura M. Pérez, Miguel Ojeda-Martínez, Nassima El Ouarie, Pablo Díaz, David Laroze, El Mustapha Feddi
pmc-10534868.description: Using first-principle calculations, we investigate the impact of strain on the electronic structures and effective masses of Janus WSTe and MoSTe monolayers. The calculations were performed using the QUANTUM-ESPRESSO package, employing the PBE and HSE06 functionals. Our results demonstrate that strain fundamentally changes the electronic structures of the Janus WSTe and MoSTe monolayers.

pmc-10632351.title: MRD negativity: considerations for older adults with multiple myeloma
pmc-10632351.creator: Hira Mian, Tanya M Wildes, Christopher P Venner, Rafael Fonseca
pmc-10632351.description: used on younger, transplant eligible patients. However, MRD testing may be equally important among older transplant-ineligible patients with MM. We argue that MRD testing may prove to be a core component in the delivery of personalized and tailored treatment among older adults with MM.

pmc-11313851.title: Constructing Heterostructured MWCNT-BN Hybrid Fillers in Electrospun TPU Films to Achieve Superior Thermal Conductivity and Electrical Insulation Properties
pmc-11313851.creator: Yang Zhang, Shichang Wang, Hong Wu, Shaoyun Guo, Alexey L Iordanskii
pmc-11313851.description: The development of thermally conductive polymer/boron nitride (BN) composites with excellent electrically insulating properties is urgently demanded for electronic devices. However, the method of constructing an efficient thermally conductive network is still challenging. In the present work, heterostructured multi-walled carbon nanotube-boron nitride (MWCNT-BN) hybrids were easily prepared using an electrostatic self-assembly method.

pmc-11519280.title: Transfer learning classification of suspicious lesions on breast ultrasound: is there room to avoid biopsies of benign lesions?
pmc-11519280.creator: Paolo De Marco, Valerio Ricciardi, Marta Montesano, Enrico Cassano, Daniela Origgi
pmc-11519280.description: BackgroundBreast cancer (BC) is the most common malignancy in women and the second cause of cancer death. In recent years, there has been a strong development in artificial intelligence (AI) applications in medical imaging for several tasks. Our aim was to evaluate the potential of transfer learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in discriminating suspicious breast lesions on ultrasound images.

pmc-11583896.creator: Philip D St John, Scott Nowicki, Robert B Tate

pmc-12543213.title: An Information App (e-TOP) to Support Parents’ Information Needs During the First Year at Home After Preterm Birth: Development and Usability Study
pmc-12543213.creator: Monique Flierman, Eline L Möller, Vincent L Vijn, Raoul H Engelbert, Martine Jeukens-Visser, Anton H van Kaam, Daniel Bossen, Sherif Badawy
pmc-12543213.description: BackgroundParents of preterm infants often face challenges in transitioning from hospital to home, requiring reliable and accessible information to support their caregiving. Mobile health interventions have the potential to supplement postdischarge education and empower parents by providing tailored, evidence-based information.

pmc-12692597.title: From Pathways to Patients in Atopic Dermatitis: Advanced Systemic Therapies
pmc-12692597.creator: Alvaro Prados-Carmona, Husein Husein-ElAhmed, Francisco José Navarro-Triviño, Ricardo Ruiz-Villaverde, Hanna Myśliwiec
pmc-12692597.description: Atopic dermatitis is the most prevalent chronic inflammatory skin disease, posing a significant individual and healthcare burden. Traditionally managed with topical agents and broad immunosuppressants, the treatment landscape has shifted significantly in recent years. This review explores the transition from immunopathogenic understanding to personalized treatment strategies through advanced systemic therapies.

pmc-12836971.title: Development and content validation of a questionnaire of activities in health promotion for primary and secondary education: PromoACTIVA-CE
pmc-12836971.creator: Isabel Antón-Solanas, Marta Callén-Galindo, Fernando Urcola-Pardo, Olga López-Dicastillo, Agurtzane Mujika, Naia Hernantes, Eva Benito-Ruiz, Edurne Zabaleta-del-Olmo, Dolors Juvinyá-Canal, María Jesús Pumar-Méndez
pmc-12836971.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to develop, refine, and assess content validity of the PromoACTIVA-CE questionnaire, designed to assess health promotion activities in primary and secondary education. The tool addresses the need for a culturally and contextually relevant instrument to systematically evaluate and support health promotion initiatives in schools.

pmc-12969002.title: A dataset of whole-genome sequencing and genomic variants for the American Shad, Alosa sapidissima, from the Neuse River, North Carolina
pmc-12969002.creator: Ella S. Adams-Herrmann, Tara Morgan, Lauren Deaner, Sönke Johnsen, Benjamin R. Wheeler, Robert R. Fitak
pmc-12969002.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Genetic data are critical for informing future conservation decisions for the American Shad, Alosa sapidissima, an economically important fish in the eastern coast of the United States. To improve genomic resources for this species, we generated more than 230 Gbp of whole-genome sequencing data from an individual American Shad collected from a hatchery with parentage from the Neuse River in North Carolina, USA.

pmc-12996985.title: Protocol for quantifying the adhesive strength of single fluorescent cells adhering to a non-fluorescent cell monolayer by fluidic force microscopy
pmc-12996985.creator: Gubesh Gunaratnam, Eugene Oh, Philipp Jung, Markus Bischoff, Wolfgang Metzger
pmc-12996985.description: Fluidic force microscopy combines the strengths of microfluidics and atomic force microscopy, allowing the analysis of cell detachment with up to several hundred nanonewton adhesion forces, without the application of chemical adhesives, which is not possible with atomic force microscopy alone.

pmc-13287309.title: Combining individual and close‐kin mark–recapture to design an effective wildlife population survey
pmc-13287309.creator: Eiren K. Jacobson, Mark V. Bravington, Rebecca L. Taylor, Irina S. Trukhanova, David L. Miller, William S. Beatty
pmc-13287309.description: Close‐kin mark–recapture (CKMR) is a promising approach for assessing population size of species that have been difficult to survey using more traditional methods. Here, we combine individual and close‐kin mark–recapture in a single modeling framework (ICKMR) and provide an example of study design using this approach for Pacific walrus (Odobenus rosmarus divergens).

pmc-13369184.title: Network architecture determines delay robustness in the spindle assembly checkpoint
pmc-13369184.creator: Bashar Ibrahim
pmc-13369184.description: The spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) ensures accurate chromosome segregation during mitosis by preventing premature activation of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C). Despite its critical role in maintaining genomic stability, most mathematical models of the SAC treat underlying biochemical processes as instantaneous, neglecting experimentally observed delays arising from molecular activation, complex assembly, and intracellular transport.

pmc-13588125.title: Impact of Oncology Patients’ Knowledge and Awareness on Emergency Visits and Hospital Admissions: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13588125.creator: Nada Alsuhebany, Shuroug A Alowais, Waad Saleh Alanazi, Taif Z Alanazi, Sarah Ibrahim Aldaghreer, Bashayer Alshehri, Nadin Almosnid, Salwa Y Hafez, Lama Alfehaid, Mashael Almuqrin, Khalid Al Sulaiman, Khalid A Alamer, Ibrahim M Asiri
pmc-13588125.description: IntroductionChemotherapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment, but is frequently accompanied by adverse effects that can affects patients’ quality of life. In Saudi Arabia, patients’ understanding of chemotherapy regimens and related toxicities is not well characterized. This study aimed to evaluate chemotherapy awareness among cancer patients and examine its association with hospital admissions and emergency department (ED) visits.

pmc-13652725.title: CAR-T TEMRA and CAR-Tregs in vivo expansion are both associated with a poor response after CD19.CAR-T therapy
pmc-13652725.creator: Luigi Carriero, Lucia Di Re, Francesco Guardalupi, Raffaella Giancola, Fabrizia Colasante, Giulia Corradi, Francesca Troiano, Noemi Michetti, Giuseppina Ricciuti, Luana Schiattone, Annalisa Natale, Nicole Santoro, Matteo Emidio Dragani, Corrado Colasante, Ida Villanova, Antonello Brattelli, Valentin
pmc-13652725.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Elsa Pennese, Mauro Di Ianni
Published: 2026

To the Editor,

Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has proven significant efficacy in B-cell malignancies with a subset of patients that fails to respond [1–3]. Several mechanisms have been proposed to account for the failure of CAR-T cell therapy, including T cell exhaustion and apoptosis [4], antigen loss [5] and resistance of cancer cells to apoptosis [6].
